newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Gains intact, WPPSS prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Gains intact, WPPSS prices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds held onto 1/2 to 3/4 point gains derived from soft morning economic data while the Washington Public Power Supply System surprised the new issue market with a $214 million refunding.
Friday's refunding marks WPPSS second visit to the market this week, and fulfills the utility's earlier plan to sell $600 million of refunding bonds.
WPPSS priced $389 million refunding bonds on Tuesday, but held off pricing the remainder because market conditions failed to match its refunding targets. That changed Friday.

"With the market up, obviously we were in a position to lower yields from the other day," Richard Kolman, vice president and manager of underwriting and syndication at lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co said Friday. "As you well know the long bond is below seven percent."
One of the advantages of a negotiated deal is the ability to react quickly to market changes, Kolman said.
"If your team is ready, you can move quickly," he said.
A quick move is less risky than if the issuer were to wait to announce a sale on Tuesday for instance, he said.

"Look at earlier in the week. Not only was there going to be a tightening, the question was how much," Kolman said. "Now all of a sudden today they are taking a tightening out of the market, so the market's volatile and will probably continue to be volatile."
The top yield on Tuesday's $389 million deal was 5.91 in 2012. Friday's tenative pricing shows a 5.85 percent in 2012. Both maturities were insured.
Back in muni cash, the market was "pretty active," a California trader said.
"We've probably taken 10 basis points off yields in most of the serials," the trader said. "Dollar bond land isn't quite as good, I've got that stuff (better by) about an 05."
Getting trades done was a struggle, however, because many holding bonds were reluctant to part with them, and marked them up beyond levels that interested buyers, he said.
"The buyers tried hard up an 05, and they couldn't buy anything so they just went home--very classic muni market," the trader said."

A trader in New York said bonds were "up dramatically," with the intermediate range improving by "a good, solid 10" basis points. The long end improved by about a nickel, and balances on deals were cleaning up fast, he said.
"A lot of the deals that were around yesterday and bonds that have been in syndicate all traded today," the trader said.

Both munis and U.S. Treasuries rose sharply after the Labor Department said its consumer price index rose 0.1 percent both overall and excluding food and energy prices. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 0.2 percent rise both overall and for the core rate.

Retail sales came in sharply below economists expectations. Sales rose 0.2 percent both overall and excluding autos in August. Economists had predicted a 0.7 percent rise, and a 0.4 percent increase excluding autos.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 1-22/32 at 113-24/32. The December T-bond contract was up 1-19/32 at 108-27/32. The MOB spread was 157 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 1-19/32 at 97-18/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
